claim: The 'Au fil de l'Our' loop starts at Our church (Paliseul), is 11.5 km with 222 m ascent (max 347 m, min 259 m), classified easy, ~3 h 9 min — the signed loop closest to the village.
quote: Distance: 11.5 km ... Maximum altitude of 347 m, minimum of 259 m, with 222 m uphill and 219 m downhill gain ... Starting Point: Church of Our (Paliseul) ... approximately 3 hours and 9 minutes

claim: Paliseul commune has 32 marked walking circuits plus 9 mountain-bike circuits on its 2021 map, sold for €7.50 at the Syndicat d'Initiatives (Grand Place 7).
quote: La nouvelle carte des promenades de Paliseul, édition 2021, contient 32 circuits pédestres balisés et 9 circuits VTT balisés

claim: The classic Tombeau du Géant family loop from Botassart is 6.5 km, easy, with free parking at the viewpoint and a small bar on-site, taking in the Lyru viewpoint and Rocher des Gattes.
quote: 6,5 km ... facile ... Un parking gratuit est disponible au point de vue du tombeau du géant ... Un petit bar au point de vue est disponible ... le point de vue de Lyru ... le rocher des Gattes

claim: An even shorter Tombeau du Géant variant via Moulin du Rivage is 4.81 km, 130 m gain, ~1 h 24, rated easy, but can be slippery after rain.
quote: Distance: 4.81 km ... Elevation Gain: 130 m ... Duration: 1 hour 24 minutes ... Easy ... requiring sturdy hiking boots as sections can be slippery, especially after rain

claim: The big 17.5 km Tombeau du Géant adventure loop has ~700 m elevation, two Semois river crossings, is hard, only feasible May–Oct in low water, parking at Moulin du Rivage.
quote: 17.5 km as a loop with approximately 700 m of elevation gain ... Two Semois river crossings ... May–Oct when water levels remain manageable ... do not underestimate how hard this hike is

claim: The Échelles de Rochehaut loop is 4.7 km, ~1 h 30, rated difficult, with metal ladders up steep cliffs; sturdy shoes required and not advised after heavy rain.
quote: Distance: 4.7 km ... 1 hour 30 minutes ... Difficile ... appropriate hiking shoes, as certain passages can be slippery ... climbing metal ladders on steep rocky cliffs

claim: The combined Échelles + Crêtes de Frahan circuit from Rochehaut is the regional benchmark hike, with hundreds of AllTrails reviews highlighting its scrambles and Frahan ridge panoramas.
quote: Rochehaut - Les Échelles - Crêtes de Frahan, Luxembourg, Belgium - 578 Reviews

claim: The Bouillon '12 viewpoints' circuit is 14.62 km with +665 m, medium difficulty, ~6 h, and chains Belvédère de Bouillon, Pic du Diable, Tombeau du Géant, Rocher du Pendu and Ramonette.
quote: Distance: 14.62 km ... Elevation Gain: +665 m ... Difficulty: Medium ... Pic du Diable (km 4.08) ... Augustins/Tombeau du Géant (km 6.54) ... Rocher du Pendu (km 8.93)

claim: Pic du Diable, a rocky belvedere over the Semois plain west of Bouillon, is a stand-alone POI reachable by several waymarked routes including an 18.7 km Belvédère d'Auclin – Pic du Diable loop (~5 h 23).
quote: From the viewpoint 'Pic du Diable' you can enjoy a sweeping view over the Semois river plains ... a difficult circuit from Bouillon called 'Belvédère d'Auclin – Le Pic du Diable' covers 18.7 km and takes about 5 hours and 23 minutes

claim: The Maison du Tourisme de Bouillon lists the canonical local viewpoints — Chaire à Prêcher (Corbion), Tombeau du Géant (Botassart), Belvédère Panorama, Rocher de Baimont/Ramonette, Frahan loop, Jambon de la Semois (Membre) and Roche à Saloru — but does not list a 'Roche à 7 heures' in Bouillon.
quote: Chaire à Prêcher - Corbion ... Tombeau du Géant - Botassart ... Belvédère Panorama - Bouillon ... Frahan & Semois Loop - Rochehaut ... Jambon de la Semois - Membre ... Roche à Saloru - Membre

claim: The famous 'Roche à Sept Heures' is in Monthermé, French Ardennes — a Meuse-valley belvedere named for the 7 o'clock sun-flash on the cliff, not a Bouillon-area site.
quote: The name Roche à Sept Heures comes from the fact that at seven o'clock, the sun illuminating this rocky spur gives it a very visible shine ... overlooks the town of Monthermé and opens a beautiful window onto the bends of the Meuse

claim: Roche aux Éperviers at Bouillon is a fitted belvedere with stairs and a safety rail above the 'longest meander created by the Semois', overlooking Botassart and Poupehan woods.
quote: improved access pathway with stairs and safety railings ... Botassart and Poupehan woodlands ... la plus longue boucle créée par la Semois

claim: GR 16 'Sentier de la Semois' is 209 km from Arlon to Monthermé, marked with the standard white-red blazes, with a 7th-edition topo-guide at €23.
quote: Total Length: 209 kilometers ... Endpoints: Arlon to Monthermé ... Seventh edition ... Price: €23.00

claim: The Trans-Semoisienne is a 184 km source-to-mouth multi-use route co-signed with GR16 white-red blazes in Belgium; its own yellow-triangle marking is for horses and MTB, and between Auby-sur-Semois and Bouillon it shortcuts the meanders via tarmac while GR16 hugs the river.
quote: 184 km total ... Volunteers maintain white-and-red blazes (GR 16 standard markings) ... a yellow horizontal triangle with the Contrat de rivière Semois/Semoy logo ... intended for equestrians and mountain bikers ... Trans-Semoisienne cuts across several Semois meanders via asphalt roads between Auby-sur-Semois and Bouillon

claim: 'Au gré de la Semois' is an easy 8.3 km riverside walk from Porte de France in Bouillon, marked red rectangle (BN #41), passing the Épine suspended footbridge to Cordemois Abbey — a strong family option.
quote: Distance: 8.3 km ... Difficulty: Easy ... Porte de France 1 à 6830 Bouillon ... longe la Semois via un magnifique sentier ... red rectangles (trail BN #41)

claim: The Parc national Vallée de la Semois runs a 2026 calendar of around sixty guided walks between April and October, useful for late-May visitors looking for ranger-led options.
quote: Un calendrier de balades guidées 2026 ... une soixantaine de sorties prévues ... entre les mois d'avril et d'octobre

claim: Récréalle in Alle-sur-Semois offers five routes ranging from 7 km Alle-Vresse (1.5 h) to 27 km Bouillon-Alle (6-7 h, experts only)
quote: Parcour 1: Alle-Vresse... 7 km... No major difficulty. Parcour 5: Bouillon-Alle... 27 km... Recommended for experts and sports people

claim: Récréalle/Kayaks La Vanne 2026 pricing: Alle-Vresse 7 km €20/person (double kayak), Alle-Bohan 17 km €28/person, shuttle included
quote: Alle-sur-Semois to Vresse-sur-Semois 7 km... Two-person kayak: €20/person. Alle-sur-Semois to Bohan 17 km Two-person kayak: €28/person

claim: Semois Kayaks (Poupehan) offers 4 km Poupehan-Frahan (1 h, from €25), 16 km Bouillon-Poupehan (3h30, from €30), and 20 km Bouillon-Frahan (5 h, from €40), all with shuttle, open March 15 - October 30
quote: Route 1: 4 km (Poupehan to Frahan)... Á partir de 25€... Route 2: 16 km (Bouillon to Poupehan)... Á partir de 30€... Route 3: 20 km (Bouillon to Frahan)... Á partir de 40€

claim: Les Epinoches in Bouillon offers Saty-Bouillon 7 km (1h30), Dohan-Bouillon 14 km (3 h), and Cugnon-Bouillon 28 km (6 h), with free minibus shuttle
quote: Saty-Bouillon 7 km 1h30... Dohan-Bouillon 14 km 3 heures... Cugnon-Bouillon 28 km 6 heures... Transport gratuit en car ou minibus

claim: Kayak Semois Ardenne 2026 list price: Poupehan-Alle 10 km €23.10/pp, Alle-Bohan 17 km €27.50/pp, Poupehan-Membre 23 km €33/pp, single-seat supplement €35
quote: Alle - Vresse 7 km 2h €38.50... Poupehan - Alle 10 km 2h €23.10... Alle - Bohan 17 km 4h €27.50... Single seat supplement: €35.00

claim: Navigation on the Semois is authorised between 2.2 and 50 m³/s; spring flow typically 15-60 m³/s with May described as ideal for sporty paddlers
quote: Spring 15–60 m³/s Often high flows post-rain... Bank blooming, wildlife nesting. Ideal for sporty paddlers. Too Low: Below 2.2 m³/s... Too High: Above 50 m³/s

claim: Récréalle confirms permitted Semois kayak flow window of 2.2-50 m³/s with green/yellow/red flag system tied to Walloon hydrological monitoring
quote: The waterlevel ( flow rate) of the Semois is between 2,2m3/s and 50m3/s... Green flag - The circulation of the kayaks is allowed

claim: The Semois between Chiny and Bouillon is class I (easy) and navigable year-round; below 35 m³/s at Membre it becomes uninteresting due to rocks
quote: A partir de 40m3/s à Membre, la navigation se fait sans toucher les cailloux... Peu intéressant en-dessous de 35m3/s... Toute l'année

claim: Self-guided castle tours last about an hour, 1.5 hours with audioguide; the esplanade has a free parking lot with around fifty spaces and additional free parking is available in town if needed.
quote: Self-guided tours last around an hour... The esplanade of Bouillon Castle has a free parking lot with around fifty spaces

claim: Falconry shows run Feb 22-Nov 11 at 11:30, 14:00 and 15:30 with an extra 17:00 show on weekends in April/May/June/September and daily in July/August; each show lasts about 30 minutes and is included in castle admission.
quote: Falconry shows... take place at 11:30 a.m., 2:00 p.m., and 3:30 p.m., with an additional 5:00 p.m. show on weekends in April, May, June, and September

claim: The Bouillon City Pass is a single combo ticket covering the Château fort, Archéoscope (Bouillon Medieval Experience) and Musée Ducal; in high season (Apr 1-Nov 11 2026) the City Pass+ adds the L'Odyssée de Lumière night show and costs €16 adult / €12 child/student.
quote: Bouillon City Pass+ (which includes the pass plus the 'L'Odyssée de Lumière' night show at the castle) costs Adults and 65+: €16 - Students and children: €12

claim: Bouillon Castle holds 4.4/5 across 1,565 TripAdvisor reviews; visitors praise the medieval atmosphere, secret passages, panoramic Semois views and falconry shows, while common complaints are the steep uphill walk and numerous stairs, occasional weather-cancelled falconry shows, and that the City Pass bundles attractions automatically.
quote: Overall Rating: 4.4 of 5 bubbles (1,565 reviews)... Steep uphill walk and numerous stairs to reach the castle... Automatic 'pass' bundling discourages single-attraction visits

claim: The Musée Ducal rates only 3.7/5 across 68 TripAdvisor reviews; visitors estimate 30-60 minutes for the visit, praise the crusades artifacts and local ironwork displays but complain about limited English signage and inflexible ticket-desk staff.
quote: Overall Rating: 3.7 out of 5 bubbles (68 reviews)... Limited English materials... Reviewers estimate 30-60 minutes for a complete visit

claim: The renovated Bouillon Medieval Experience (Archéoscope) scores 4.3/5 on TripAdvisor with praise for immersive audiovisual scenography, multilingual personal-headphone audio guides and friendly staff, but reviewers note the content is heavily about the First Crusade rather than Godefroid himself and recommend it for ages 9+.
quote: Overall Rating: 4.3 out of 5 stars (19 reviews)... Audio guide system allowing multilingual access simultaneously via personal headphones... it's better for ages 9+

claim: The Tombeau du Géant at Botassart is classified as 'exceptional heritage of Wallonia' — a wooded hill in a meander of the Semois forming a monumental sarcophagus shape, and is one of Belgium's most photographed landscapes.
quote: The Giant's Tomb is an exceptional geomorphosite classified as 'exceptional heritage of Wallonia' located in Botassart, municipality of Bouillon

claim: Free parking is available at the Botassart belvedere with the viewpoint reachable in a few minutes' walk without difficulty; refreshment bar and restrooms only open in July-August, and access is free 24/7 year-round.
quote: Free parking is available on-site in Botassart... accessible from the parking lot 'in a few minutes' walk, without difficulty'... Refreshment bar and restrooms available in high season (July-August)

claim: The Pont de Liège in Bouillon was first mentioned in 1069 as a wooden bridge linking Germany to France, rebuilt in stone in 1598 and reinforced by Vauban in 1680; the current bridge dates from 1951 and sits opposite the Hôtel de la Poste.
quote: Le Pont de Liège... face à l'Hôtel de la Poste... première mention en 1069... reconstruit en pierre en 1598... renforcé par Vauban en 1680... pont actuel date de 1951

claim: Bouillon's architectural promenade starts from the tourist office in the former Sépulcrines convent (1626) on the Quai des Saulx, follows Boulevard Heynen along the Semois, crosses the Pont de Liège and loops back below the castle ramparts.
quote: promenade architecturale... Quai des Saulx... ancien couvent des Sépulcrines (1626)... boulevard Heynen le long de la Semois... Pont de Liège

claim: The Botassart viewpoint offers a plunging view of the Semois meander winding around a wooded promontory.
quote: The Botassart viewpoint offers a plunging view of the meander, showcasing the Semois making the most of the relief, constantly winding back and forth.

claim: The Rochehaut panorama over Frahan stretches along 300m of road with a balustrade and free binoculars, classified as a major heritage site of Wallonia.
quote: The viewpoint is arranged along 300 meters of length, along the asphalt road, and impresses with the expansiveness of the landscape opening to viewers. There is a balustrade with free binoculars.

claim: The Frahan viewpoint has been classified as a 'Jewel of Wallonia' since 2015 and is one of the most photographed viewpoints in Belgium.
quote: The site has been classified as a 'Jewel of Wallonia' since 2015 and has become one of the most photographed viewpoints in Belgium.

claim: The Frahan loop trail from Laviot through the Vallée de la Semois National Park is about 9.5 km with 300 m elevation gain, taking 2.5-3 hours.
quote: The Frahan Loop starts in Laviot and takes you through the Vallée de la Semois National Park, following the river to the Corbeaux viewpoint and the village of Frahan. This loop covers 5.9 miles with an elevation gain of 1,000 feet

claim: The Semois Tobacco Route is a two-circuit driving itinerary across Vresse and Bouillon communes highlighting the tobacco-growing heritage that shaped the valley for over a century.
quote: The Semois Tobacco Route is a circuit made up of 2 routes to be followed by car in the communes of Vresse and Bouillon, aiming to highlight the last witnesses of tobacco growing

claim: Vresse-sur-Semois became a 'village of painters' in the early 20th century when José Chaidron founded the Vresse School around 1920; the former Hotel La Glycine now hosts the tourism office and art exhibitions.
quote: In the early 20th century, Vresse-sur-Semois became the village of painters, with José Chaidron founding the 'Vresse School' around 1920... Vresse-sur-Semois is known as a 'Village of Art,' with the former Hotel La Glycine serving as the local tourism office

claim: Laforêt was awarded the 'Most Beautiful Villages of Wallonia' label on 7 October 1955 and remains one of the rare southern Ardenne villages to keep its original character.
quote: This label was awarded on October 7, 1955, and is well-deserved as Laforêt is one of the rare villages of southern Ardenne that has retained its former character.

claim: Laforêt's rustic Pont de Claies — woven hornbeam-branch panels on frail pillars in the river — is reopened each summer between mid-June and mid-September.
quote: Laforêt is famous for its illustrious 'Pont de Claies' on the Semois, a rustic bridge made up of panels woven with hornbeam branches placed on frail pillars in the riverbed itself. In summer, you can cross the famous 'Pont de Claies', which is reopened between mid-June and mid-September

claim: Alle-sur-Semois' Récréalle leisure complex has a 300-space private car park and free return mini-buses for kayak descents.
quote: The facility has a private parking area with 300 places, and free mini-buses are provided for your return trip when doing the Semois kayak descent.

claim: Top-rated Alle-sur-Semois attractions include Ardois'alle (a former slate-mine guided tour, 4.5/5) and Kayaks La Vanne (4.9/5), with Récréalle offering 7-27 km kayak descents plus bowling.
quote: Ardois'alle (4.5/5 stars) - A guided tour through a former slate mine... Kayaks La Vanne (4.9/5 stars)... Récréalle offers kayaking descent options (7, 12, 22, or 27 km routes along the Semois River), plus bowling and playground activities.

claim: The 52nd Festival des Arts de la rue at Chassepierre runs 15-16 August 2026 with 50+ street-arts companies from Belgium, France, Spain, Netherlands and Germany.
quote: Over two days, some of Europe's finest young artists, musicians, dancers and puppeteers entertain the crowds at the festival's beautiful riverside hub, on the banks of the pretty Semois river. Over 50 companies

claim: Chassepierre is one of the Most Beautiful Villages of Wallonia, sitting on a rocky spur where the Semois 'is on stage'.
quote: Chassepierre, the Semois is on stage - Most Beautiful Villages of Wallonia

claim: Mortehan's classified old cemetery, decommissioned in 1899 and listed as a historical monument in 1972, is the village's signature draw alongside its slate houses and old mill.
quote: The old cemetery in Mortehan carries visitors into another world... This cemetery was decommissioned in 1899 and was classified as a historical monument on November 20, 1972.

claim: Dohan (179 inhabitants) features an early-17th-century schist-and-sandstone castle on a rocky bluff and the Point de vue de la Schevauchée over its bridge.
quote: A castle was constructed in the early 17th century, presenting itself as an imposing manor in schist and sandstone partially rendered, built on a rocky foundation dominating the Semois about twenty meters high... The most prominent viewpoint is the Point de vue de la Schevauchée

claim: Poupehan sits in one of the most spectacular Semois meanders and is the access point for Les Échelles de Rochehaut — a steep ladder-equipped trail along schist cliffs.
quote: Poupehan is nestled in one of the most spectacular meanders of the Semois... Les Échelles de Rochehaut (The Ladders of Rochehaut) is a dizzying trail equipped with metal ladders, climbing up the side of schist cliffs, accessible from Poupehan via the GR16.

claim: Membre-sur-Semois is reached by a family-friendly 3-hour Alle-Membre kayak descent featuring grey herons, beaver dam sites and the Jambon Belvedere Corten-steel platform.
quote: Arrival in Membre-sur-Semois, a picturesque village with a view of the Jambon Belvedere (Corten steel platform)... The Alle-Membre route takes 3 hours, is ideal with the family

claim: Parking in Bouillon is free citywide but fills up during peak-season weekends and major events like the Fête Médiévale and Fête de la Chasse.
quote: Only during top events (e.g. Hunting Festival - Fête de la Chasse, the Medieval Festival - Fête Médiévale) and on weekends during the real high season it is difficult to find a parking space. However, parking is free in the entire city.

claim: The Luxembourg-province Points-Noeuds bike network covers ~2,500 km, 530 numbered nodes across all 44 communes with about 12,000 signage panels; 85% paved and 15% unpaved, designed for VTC rather than road bikes.
quote: 85% of roads are paved (asphalt, concrete...) and 15%

claim: Two signed Points-Noeuds loops from the Bouillon tourism office explicitly pass through Our village: 'Nature et Paysages 3' (29 km, intermediate, 480 m D+) and 'Villages d'Ardenne 2' (23 km, easy, 310 m D+), with nodes PN 59 located near Our and PN 61 by Ferme des Sureaux.
quote: Nature et Paysages - 3 ... 29 km ... 480 m ... Passes through Our village

claim: Three featured Points-Noeuds loops in the Bouillon region: 'Virée Pittoresque' (19 km, 392 m D+, medium) from Bouillon, 'Immersion au Coeur des Forêts' (26 km, 540 m D+) from Bertrix, and 'Entre Vallées et Plateaux' (55 km, 943 m D+, hard) from Vresse-sur-Semois passing Laforêt.
quote: Virée Pittoresque Autour de Bouillon ... 19km ... 392m ... Medium

claim: RAVeL ligne 163 runs 57 km Gouvy–Bastogne–Libramont; the Gouvy-Bastogne leg (27.5 km) is finished asphalt RAVeL, while the Bastogne–Libramont leg (29.5 km) is still a 'pre-RAVeL' rideable on a mountain bike, sitting above 500 m on the Meuse/Rhine watershed ridge.
quote: Stage 2 (Bastogne to Libramont): 29.5 km - Currently a 'pre-RAVeL' (under development)

claim: Regional cycling route W7 (Sur la Route des Ardennes) is fully signed through Sainte-Ode, Libramont, Libin, Bertrix, Paliseul and Bouillon — giving Our a direct waymarked link from Paliseul down to Bouillon — and W5 is signed Bouillon–Corbion, eventually to Vresse and Gedinne.
quote: the towns crossed (Sainte-Ode, Libramont, Libin, Bertrix, Paliseul and Bouillon) ... signpost and mark the sections of the last two stages of the W7 regional cycling route

claim: The Bike Trail Center de Bouillon offers a 42 km enduro circuit with ~1,200 m elevation gain plus five short specific MTB loops graded blue/red/black like ski slopes, passing Cordemois, Moulin de l'Épine, Poupehan, Frahan, Rochehaut, Botassart and Sensenruth; two beginner lines exist for children aged 5–10.
quote: 42 km enduro course with approximately 1,200 m of elevation gain ... Five shorter trail circuits ... ski-slope color system

claim: Bouillon's trail center was Belgium's first officially-sanctioned trail building project, backed by local authorities and the forestry department; trails use natural terrain with sub-50 cm width and berms/jumps from fallen branches.
quote: marking Belgium's first officially-sanctioned trail building weekend

claim: The Pays de Bouillon publishes signed gravel circuits including Gravel Bouillon-Bertrix (53 km), Gravel Bertrix-Paliseul (35 km, starting from Paliseul), Gravel Bièvre (37 km), Gravel Vresse-sur-Semois (39 km) plus Herbeumont (31–38 km) and Gribomont (31 km) loops.
quote: Gravel Bertrix Paliseul ... Distance: 35 km ... Starting point: Paliseul

claim: Komoot lists 80+ MTB trails around Vresse-sur-Semois including a hard 47.4 km Saint-Lambert loop with 930 m D+ from Vresse, a moderate 31.8 km Bohan loop with 450 m D+, and an easy 8.6 km Mouzaive loop with 180 m D+ — covering all difficulty levels.
quote: Along the Semois - Saint-Lambert Bridge loop from Vresse-sur-Semois ... 47.4 km ... Hard ... 930m

claim: Cap Semois in Vresse-sur-Semois (Rue du Perré 79-80) rents Trek 500W Bosch e-MTBs at €50 half-day / €80 full day and regular VTTs at €28/€30, with 40 km turbo / 100+ km eco range, no deposit, helmet free, and itineraries of 14/20/35 km on 1,000+ km of marked trails.
quote: Half-day (4.5 hours): €28 (standard VTT), €50 (e-bike) ... Full day: €30 (standard VTT), €80 (e-bike)

claim: Récréalle in Alle-sur-Semois rents e-bikes at €25 (2-4 h) / €35 (1 day) / €60 (2 days) and regular VTTs at €25 half-day / €30 full day / €35 for 24 h, with access to several fully-marked MTB trails directly from the leisure base.
quote: E-bikes ... 2-4 hours: €25.00 ... 1 day (8 hours): €35.00 ... Mountain Bikes (VTT) ... Half-day: €25.00 ... Full day: €30.00

claim: The Maison du Tourisme de Bouillon coordinates a dense network of rental shops covering the Our/Paliseul area — Récréalle and L'Ami Pierre in Alle, Cap Semois in Vresse, Arde-Bike in Rienne, Cellier du Baudet in Bertrix, Sports in Lux in Herbeumont and AmuSemois/E-trott in Bouillon — for VTT, e-VTT and standard bikes.
quote: Location VTT Récréalle (Alle) ... Location VTT L'Ami Pierre (Alle) ... E-bike location Sensenruth ... Cap Semois - location VTT (Vresse-sur-Semois) ... Arde-Bike (Rienne)

claim: The 2021 Paliseul walking map (€7.50 from Syndicat d'Initiatives) contains 32 signed hiking circuits plus 9 marked VTT circuits covering the commune that contains Our.
quote: La nouvelle carte des promenades de Paliseul, édition 2021, contient 32 circuits pédestres balisés et 9 circuits VTT balisés

claim: Euro Space Center in Transinne (~30 min from Paliseul) is open 9:00 to 16:00 (last entry) with visits lasting about 6 hours, and booking online saves €2 per ticket.
quote: Open from 9:00am to 4:00pm (last entry) ... Book in advance and save €2 per ticket!

claim: Euro Space Center reviews are mixed: families with kids 8-11 enjoy gravity simulators, moonwalk and virtual missions, but some say ages 6-12 found it boring and prices excessive for the quality.
quote: Activities are engaging and interactive, designed for adults and children, from gravity simulators to training tests to virtual space missions

claim: Grottes de Han 2026 prices: Cave only adult €29 / child 4-11 €22; PassHan (cave + wildlife park) adult €41.50 / child €31.50; under-4s free.
quote: GROTTE : adulte 29€ - enfant (4-11 ans) 22€ ... PASSHAN : adulte 41,50€ - enfant (4-11 ans) 31,50€

claim: Grottes de Han is open daily in late May 2026 except 11, 12 and 18 May, with the Cave Discovery tour lasting 1h15 and the longer Cave Journey 2 hours over 510 steps.
quote: Mai : ouvert tous les jours (sauf les 11, 12 et 18 Mai = fermé) ... 'Cave Discovery' dure 1h15 ... 'Cave Journey' dure 2 heures avec 510 marches

claim: Bouillon Castle entry is €7 adult / €5 child 4-12, and the Bouillon City Pass+ (April-November 2026) combining castle, Musée Ducal, Medieval Experience and the Odyssée de Lumière light show is €16 adult / €12 child.
quote: Individual castle admission: Adults €7, 65+ €6, Students €5.50, Children (4-12 years) €5 ... Bouillon City Pass+ ... Adults and 65+ €16

claim: Bouillon Medieval Experience is a fully indoor immersive show in a former Sepulcrines convent, lasting 30-45 minutes with audio guides in FR/NL/DE/EN, praised for scenography but criticised for limited seating.
quote: immersive attraction that takes you back to the 11th century through the latest audiovisual technologies

claim: The Archéoscope Godefroid de Bouillon, housed in a 17th-century convent next to the castle, runs a multilingual film every 35 minutes followed by a walk-through dark room with a replica of Godefroid's Jerusalem tomb.
quote: Visits start every 35 minutes with a multilingual film, after which you walk through the screen into a darkened space

claim: The Musée du Tabac de la Semois in Corbion (Vresse-sur-Semois) operates by appointment only via +32 61 46 81 29 and documents the local Semois tobacco heritage that made the region famous.
quote: Le Musée du Tabac de la Semois ... +32 61 46 81 29

claim: Orval Abbey (~1h drive) is open June-September 9:30-18:30, with a 2-hour visit covering the Cistercian ruins, the Caves Dewez museum, the brewery exhibition in the 17th-century Communs Abraham, and a medicinal-plant pharmacy garden; the working brewery itself opens only on special Open Door days.
quote: In June, July, August and September, Orval is open from 9:30 to 18:30 ... the brewery is only open to visitors on special Open Door days

claim: Basilique Saint-Hubert (~35 min from Paliseul) is open daily 10:00-18:00 from Easter to All Saints with free entry, €2 guided tours, and a €3 reservable attic tour.
quote: open daily from Easter to All Saints' Day (10:00–18:00) ... guided tours available for €2 per person and access to the attic areas available after reservation for €3

claim: Brasserie Lupulus in Bovigny/Courtil (Gouvy) runs guided tours including a tasting and souvenir glass, daily during Belgian school holidays, restricted to visitors over 16 unless arranged in advance.
quote: Only individuals over 16 years old can be registered for tours ... Tours are open every day during Belgian school holidays

claim: Brasserie de Bertinchamps near Gembloux offers small-group 1-hour brewery tours at 10:30 on Saturdays and Sundays for €6 including a gallopin tasting, with an attached restaurant La Table de Bertinchamps.
quote: The brewery tour lasts 1 hour and takes place in small groups on Saturdays and Sundays at 10:30 am, booking required, with a price of €6 including a gallopin at the end

claim: Brasserie de la Lesse near Rochefort offers 40-minute brewery tours ending with a tasting on the café terrace, at €12/adult with tasting or €7 without, bookable online.
quote: 12€ par adulte avec dégustation, et 7€ par enfant (à partir de 12 ans) sans dégustation ... visites durent environ 40 minutes

claim: Brasserie Sainte-Hélène in Florenville (relocated from Ethe in 2016) only accepts brewery visits by appointment for groups of 5 to 50 people with 15 days' notice.
quote: Visits are by appointment for groups of 5 to 50 people, with reservations required 15 days in advance

claim: Brasserie de Bouillon opens to groups of 8+ by booking; solo visitors can otherwise stop at Le Marché de Nathalie in Bouillon town centre which stocks over 300 Belgian beer labels.
quote: open year-round for group visits of a minimum of 8 people ... Le Marché de Nathalie shop in the city centre ... over 300 labels for sale

claim: La Ferme des Fées at Les Hayons near Bouillon is a free-admission indoor attraction showcasing handmade 1/4-scale figurines of fairies, witches and 19th-century Ardennes life, open Thursday-Saturday 10:00-12:30 and 13:30-18:00.
quote: handcrafted and hand-painted figurines at 1/4 scale ... Thursday-Saturday from 10:00 AM - 12:30 PM and 1:30 PM - 6:00 PM

claim: Ardois'Alle in Alle-sur-Semois (≈20 min from Paliseul) is a former slate mine converted into a museum showcasing the region's slate-quarrying history, listed on the Réseau Ardoise d'Ardenne trail.
quote: An old slate mine in Alle-sur-Semois was also turned into a museum to showcase the region's history
